children.value: > Fact From Story Jeremy Howe played out the grand final in pain after he was floored by a bone-crunching knock to the ribs from Lions forward Charlie Cameron during the last quarter.
> > Fact From Story This pain was tolerable by comparison, and he got up and played out the match, helping Collingwood hold on to a four-point win in one of the great grand finals.
> > > Fact From Story Howe said “I’ve got six months to get them right. I can tolerate the pain for now. I bounced out of bed regardless.” | Fact From Story
> > > Fact From Story Howe told Channel Nine on Sunday "The ribs are incredibly sore but I think if we lost they’d be sorer. | Fact From Story
> > > Commonsense Knowledge People are willing to endure pain for something they value. | Commonsense Knowledge
> > Commonsense Knowledge A player will keep playing as long as they feel they are helping their team.
> Commonsense Knowledge A player can continue to play even with an injury if they are able to tolerate the pain.
